evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Molecular tumor profiling revealed a loss of heterozygosity at GPR161 in all affected MBSHH tumors, atypical somatic copy number landscapes, and no additional somatic driver events.

nodes.description: Without GPR161, processing of GLI3 to its repressor form falls and Hedgehog target genes are expressed without ligand, before Purkinje cells begin secreting Sonic hedgehog. The lesion acts on the PKA-GLI3 repressor arm and is distinct from the PTCH1 and SUFU lesions of nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Irrespective of Shh production in the cerebellum, Gpr161 deletion increased downstream activity of the Shh pathway by restricting Gli3-mediated repression, causing more extensive generation and proliferation of GC progenitors.

evidence.reference_title: The ciliary G-protein-coupled receptor Gpr161 negatively regulates the Sonic hedgehog pathway via cAMP signaling.
evidence.snippet: Complete loss of Gpr161 in mouse causes midgestation lethality and increased Shh signaling in the neural tube, phenocopying Tulp3/IFT-A mutants.

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.

evidence.reference_title: GPR161 / GPR161-related medulloblastoma predisposition (Strong)
evidence.snippet: Five variants (missense, in-frame indel, nonsense, frameshift) that have been reported in seven probands in two publications (PMIDs: 31609649, 39184053) are included in this curation.

nodes.description: A heterozygous constitutional GPR161 variant, protein-truncating in most probands and a predicted damaging missense in one, removes one functional copy of a ciliary G protein-coupled receptor. GPR161 signals constitutively to raise cAMP and anchors type I protein kinase A regulatory subunits, and its PKA-binding site is required for it to keep the Hedgehog pathway repressed.

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: We identified heterozygous germline mutations in the G protein-coupled receptor 161 (GPR161) gene in six patients with infant-onset medulloblastoma (median age, 1.5 years).

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Four patients were found to harbor GPR161 protein-truncating variants and one patient was a carrier of a predicted damaging missense variant (SJMB054).

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: Two patients (MB11_06 and SJMB335) shared the same frameshift mutation as that of the index patient; kinship analysis demonstrated that all three patients were unrelated.

evidence.snippet: Constitutive Gpr161 activity increases cAMP levels and represses Shh signaling by determining the processing of Gli3 to its repressor form.

evidence.reference_title: Gpr161 anchoring of PKA consolidates GPCR and cAMP signaling.
evidence.snippet: We show that Gpr161 functions as a selective high-affinity AKAP for type I PKA regulatory subunits (RI).

evidence.snippet: By contrast, a protein kinase A-binding site in the GPR161 C terminus is critical in suppressing GLI2 ciliary accumulation.

evidence.snippet: Gpr161 restricts GC progenitor production by preventing premature and Shh-dependent pathway activity, highlighting the importance of basal pathway suppression in tumorigenesis.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, earlier deletion of Gpr161 during embryogenesis increased tumor incidence and severity.

nodes.description: SHH-activated, TP53-wildtype medulloblastoma diagnosed in infancy or early childhood: median 1.5 years in the six carriers of the defining series, with every truncating-variant carrier diagnosed before 3 years. Five of the six tumors fell in the SHH-beta infant subtype, though that enrichment was not significant. A further carrier with a nonsense variant and SHH medulloblastoma was found by germline exome sequencing of a pediatric brain tumor cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
evidence.snippet: GPR161 mutations were exclusively associated with the sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (MBSHH) subgroup and accounted for 5% of infant MBSHH cases in our cohorts.

evidence.reference_title: Germline GPR161 Mutations Predispose to Pediatric Medulloblastoma.

nodes.description: GPR161-deficient granule progenitors give rise to SHH-activated medulloblastoma. No other somatic driver is shared across carrier tumors, which supports GPR161 loss as sufficient for initiation. Mouse tumors after Gpr161 loss are milder than after Ptch1 loss, consistent with weaker pathway induction.

evidence.reference_title: Basal Suppression of the Sonic Hedgehog Pathway by the G-Protein-Coupled Receptor Gpr161 Restricts Medulloblastoma Pathogenesis.
evidence.snippet: The severity and extent of tumorigenesis is weaker than with respect to Ptch1 conditional knockout mice (Yang et al., 2008) because Shh pathway induction upon Gpr161 depletion is weaker than upon Smo activation (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2013).

nodes.description: The wild-type GPR161 allele is lost in the tumor in every carrier studied: in five of six by copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity of chromosome 1q and in one by a focal deletion of the whole gene. Among 226 SHH medulloblastomas, 1q copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity occurred only in GPR161 carriers.
